browserVisibleComparison.label: 224 MB balanced sampled file
browserVisibleComparison.measurement: file selection to first flamegraph paint
browserVisibleComparison.note: The repeated browser-visible benchmark now leads the public story: the Rust/WASM path reaches first flamegraph almost twice as fast while UI/render overhead stays roughly flat.

syntheticComparisons.label: 11.3 MB
syntheticComparisons.note: Once append-order nodes cross the boundary as typed arrays, the Rust path stops paying the old JS object-serialization penalty.

syntheticComparisons.label: 28.1 MB
syntheticComparisons.note: The optimized boundary keeps scaling cleanly once the sampled importer has real work to do.

syntheticComparisons.label: 56.1 MB
syntheticComparisons.note: This is now the clearest repeated apples-to-apples proof point: the Rust path wins decisively on both time and memory.

syntheticComparisons.label: 112.1 MB
syntheticComparisons.note: Largest direct head-to-head sampled import currently captured in one process for both engines.

largestHeadToHead.label: 112.1 MB
largestHeadToHead.note: The largest sampled import where both engines completed head to head in the same benchmark run.

warmExperimentalLargest.label: 112.1 MB
warmExperimentalLargest.note: After module initialization, repeated experimental imports stay fast and memory-light even at the 1M-sample size.

limitCases.label: 112.1 MB legacy repeated run
limitCases.detail: A three-run legacy-only sequence on the 1M-sample synthetic file exhausted an 8 GB Node heap after two imports.

limitCases.label: 56.1 MB parity canonicalization
limitCases.detail: The parity path in the benchmark harness hit RangeError: Invalid string length while canonicalizing a 500k-sample synthetic import, so the larger synthetic rows are recorded with `--skip-parity=1`.

limitCases.label: Tiny sampled fixture cold start
limitCases.detail: On the smallest built-in sampled fixture, wasm startup can still outweigh the importer win. The strongest public demos are medium and large sampled files.
